title: Emergency Credentials and Licensure Compacts: How Districts Hire Faster
metaTitle: Emergency Teaching Credentials and Licensure Compacts
description: Emergency permits, provisional licenses, reciprocity and the interstate compacts for teachers, SLPs, OTs, PTs and school psychologists, cited to each board.
answer: A district gets an out-of-state or not-yet-certified educator working legally in 3 ways: an emergency or provisional credential the district requests, a full license through reciprocity or the teacher compact, or a compact privilege that, where live, can issue in minutes. None is automatic: Colorado's board review of an emergency authorization can add up to 60 days.
keyTakeaways: Under 34 CFR 300.156, special education teachers and related service providers cannot hold credentials waived on an emergency, temporary or provisional basis.
The Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact map lists 14 enacting states, and Pennsylvania announced it had officially joined on August 6, 2026.
Enacted is not issuing: the ASLP-IC is enacted in 37 jurisdictions, but privileges are open in 6 states.
The PT Compact is issuing in all 38 member states, including Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland.
Colorado's State Board must approve each emergency authorization, which can add up to 60 days.
bodyHtml:
What is the difference between an emergency permit, a provisional license, a compact license and reciprocity?

An emergency permit is requested by the district for one vacancy and one school year. A provisional or conditional license runs 2 to 5 years while the educator finishes requirements, a compact license or privilege is applied for by the educator on the strength of a home-state license, and full reciprocity is a standard license earned with an out-of-state credential and experience. The table lays them side by side.

RouteWho appliesTypical documentsWhat the educator can doHow long it lasts
Emergency permit or certificateThe district. In Pennsylvania, the chief school administrator of the LEABachelor's degree transcript, proof the vacancy was posted, enrollment in a preparation programFill a named vacancy. In New Jersey, only in the district that requested itAbout 1 school year: Pennsylvania through the last day of summer school, New Jersey to July 31, Delaware to June 30
Provisional, conditional or temporary licenseThe district, for a new hireDegree, an out-of-state license or completed program, test scores still pendingServe as teacher of record while finishing the state's requirements2 to 5 years: New Jersey provisional up to 2 years, renewable once; Maryland temporary professional 2 years, conditional 5 years
Compact license or privilegeThe educator or providerAn unencumbered home-state license, a background check, a jurisprudence exam where the state requires onePractice as a fully licensed professional. A compact privilege is equivalent to a licensePrivileges expire with the home-state license and are renewed after it
Full reciprocityThe educatorA valid out-of-state license, verified experience, state test scores unless an exception appliesHold the state's standard or initial license with no conditionsThe state's normal license term, for example 5 years for a Maryland Initial Professional license

The district carries the emergency and provisional routes. The educator carries the compact and reciprocity routes, and only those 2 produce a credential federal special education rules accept without conditions.

Each seat type's state rules sit on our Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware staffing pages, and Pennsylvania's permit types are broken down in our PDE emergency permit guide.

How do the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact and the health compacts speed up school hiring?

A compact lets a professional licensed in one member state work in another without a new license from scratch. Enacting a compact and issuing under it are different events, and several compacts that cover school seats are enacted widely but issuing in a handful of states. Status is as each compact's site showed it on November 18, 2026.

CompactWho it coversEnacted, as publishedIssuing yet?
Interstate Teacher Mobility CompactTeachers with an unencumbered license that required a bachelor's degree and a state-approved program14 states marked enacted on the compact map, including Pennsylvania and Delaware; Mississippi enacted with changes and not admittedPennsylvania is applying it now: its application page lists 13 member states whose certificates get a streamlined review
Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Interstate Compact (ASLP-IC)Speech-language pathologists and audiologists37 jurisdictions: 36 states and 1 territoryRegistration open in 6 states: Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Ohio, Tennessee and West Virginia. Delaware and Maryland have enacted it but are not issuing; Pennsylvania and New Jersey have bills pending
Occupational Therapy Licensure CompactOccupational therapists and OT assistants11 states accepting applications plus 26 members not yet acceptingIn 11 states, including Maryland since April 15, 2026. Pennsylvania and Delaware: not yet
Physical Therapy CompactPhysical therapists and PT assistants38 member states, plus 3 enacted and not yet issuingYes in all 38, including Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey and Pennsylvania
Counseling CompactLicensed professional counselors who can independently assess, diagnose and treat11 live states, plus 29 states and DC completing the steps to issueYes in 11 states, including Ohio and Tennessee
Interstate Compact for School PsychologistsSchool psychologists with an active, unencumbered license in a member state10 states on the compact map, including Delaware and MarylandNo. The compact is in the process of becoming operational
Nurse Licensure CompactNurses holding a multistate license43 jurisdictionsYes. Pennsylvania implemented July 7, 2025; New Jersey November 15, 2021; Delaware and Maryland January 19, 2018

Teachers

The Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact works differently from the health compacts. A teacher with an eligible license applies to the receiving state and gets "the closest equivalent license" without additional materials, state-specific exams or added coursework, and goes through that state's background check (source: Council of State Governments, ITMC FAQs). An eligible license cannot be restricted, probationary, provisional, substitute or temporary, so a teacher on an emergency permit back home does not qualify. The compact map lists 14 enacting states, and Mississippi as enacted with material language changes and not admitted (source: Council of State Governments, ITMC compact map). Pennsylvania announced it had officially joined on August 6, 2026 (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, newsroom release), and its application page now tells teachers certified in Alabama, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Kansas, Kentucky, Nebraska, Nevada, Oklahoma, Oregon, Utah, Virginia and Washington: "You don't need to do anything extra when applying" (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Out-of-State Educators, Pathway 3).

Related service providers

Where a health compact is live, the wait is short: the Counseling Compact says a privilege "can be obtained in a matter of minutes" (source: Counseling Compact Commission, counselingcompact.gov). Under the ASLP-IC, a compact privilege "is equivalent to a license," and 37 jurisdictions have enacted it, with privileges open in 6 states (source: ASLP-IC Commission, aslpcompact.gov). The OT Compact warns that a practitioner "cannot practice in an OTC state under the OT Compact, even if that state has enacted OTC legislation" until that state opens applications and approves one (source: OT Compact, otcompact.gov). Its application page lists 11 states accepting and 26 members not yet accepting (source: OT Compact, Application and Map). The PT Compact is furthest along: 38 member states are actively issuing and accepting privileges (source: PT Compact, Compact Map). Asked whether a licensed school psychologist can use it now, the school psychologist compact answers "No, not at this time" (source: Council of State Governments, Interstate Compact for School Psychologists). Colorado reports its commissioners met in January 2026 to begin writing the rules (source: Colorado Department of Education, Interstate Compact for School Psychologists).

Two compacts cover the clinical license, not the school credential. The Counseling Compact covers counselors licensed to independently assess, diagnose and treat (source: Counseling Compact Commission, counselingcompact.gov), while school counselor certificates come from education departments in Delaware and New Jersey (source: Delaware Administrative Code, 1506, 7.2.1) (source: New Jersey Department of Education, Educational Services Personnel). The Nurse Licensure Compact covers the nursing license in 43 jurisdictions (source: NCSBN, Nurse Licensure Compact) (source: NCSBN, NLC implementation map), and Pennsylvania and New Jersey both treat school nurse as a separate education credential (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, CSPG 13) (source: New Jersey Department of Education, Educational Services Personnel). For a school nurse or school counselor, plan on both.

What does IDEA allow for special education teachers and related services?

IDEA closes the emergency route for special education teachers and related service providers. Under 34 CFR 300.156, each public school special education teacher must hold full state certification and must not have "had special education certification or licensure requirements waived on an emergency, temporary, or provisional basis" (source: eCFR, 34 CFR 300.156(c)(1)(ii)).

The same section sets the related services standard. Related services personnel must meet the state's certification or licensing requirements for their discipline and must not have had those requirements "waived on an emergency, temporary, or provisional basis" (source: eCFR, 34 CFR 300.156(b)(2)). That is why a compact privilege matters for speech, OT and PT seats: it is a license, not a waiver.

There is one door for teachers. A teacher in an alternate route program counts as certified if the teacher receives sustained, intensive, classroom-focused professional development, has intensive supervision or a mentor, serves "for a specified period of time not to exceed three years," and shows satisfactory progress (source: eCFR, 34 CFR 300.156(c)(2)). States build their rules around this. Maryland's conditional special education license lasts 3 years and requires the same supervision and mentoring (source: Code of Maryland Regulations, 13A.12.02.02F). Delaware issues a certificate of eligibility, not an emergency certificate, to special education teachers, and bars specialists on emergency certificates from providing related services (source: Delaware Administrative Code, 14 DE Admin. Code 1506, 1.2 and 7.2.2). Colorado does not issue emergency authorizations for special education or special services endorsements at all (source: Colorado Department of Education, Emergency Authorization Packet).

For these seats, the fast route is a fully credentialed provider, not a permit. Our related services staffing page covers how we fill speech, OT, PT and school psychology seats. If a seat stays open, the IEP minutes still come due, and what an unfilled classroom costs puts a number on that.

How do staffing partners clear out-of-state educators before day one?

A specialist staffing partner clears the credential and the background checks before the educator is presented, so your start date is not waiting on paperwork. The work runs in 4 steps, each set by a rule your district already follows.

  1. Match the route to the seat. A special education or related services seat needs a full license or a compact privilege under 34 CFR 300.156. A general education seat can use reciprocity or a compact license.
  2. Verify the license at the source. Compact privileges can be checked in the shared data system. The Counseling Compact notes that entities "can also verify your privilege" online, and that a privilege expires on the same date as the home-state license (source: Counseling Compact Commission, counselingcompact.gov).
  3. Run the state's clearances. Pennsylvania requires a State Police criminal history record, a Department of Human Services child abuse report and an FBI report from school hires and independent contractors who will have direct contact with children, each no more than 5 years old at hire (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Background Checks). New Jersey's Office of Student Protection runs checks through the State Police and the FBI for school applicants and authorized vendors (source: New Jersey Department of Education, Criminal History Review).
  4. Track every expiration date. An OT Compact privilege expires when the home-state license expires, and it must be bought again after each renewal (source: OT Compact, Application and Map).

Pennsylvania lets a school hire provisionally for up to 90 days while checks are pending, but the person may not work alone with children (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Background Checks). A partner who finishes the checks first spares you that arrangement. The 3 Pennsylvania clearances are explained in our Act 34 and 151 guide.

What are the common credentialing bottlenecks, and how do you avoid them?

Most delays come from 5 places, and each can be checked before an offer goes out.

  • State tests. Pennsylvania requires its own content tests for out-of-state applicants unless a testing exception applies, and says "No other tests can be substituted" for Pathway 2 (source: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Out-of-State Educators). Maryland requires a reading instruction test or an observed attestation for special education, elementary, early childhood and ESOL candidates on an out-of-state license (source: Code of Maryland Regulations, 13A.12.02.03). Ask for scores at the first interview.
  • Experience verification. New Jersey's standard certificate by reciprocity needs 2 effective years within 3 consecutive years on its Record of Professional Experience form (source: New Jersey Department of Education, Reciprocity). Send the form on day one.
  • Board calendars. Colorado's State Board must approve every emergency authorization, which can add up to 60 days (source: Colorado Department of Education, Emergency Authorization Packet).
  • Enacted is not issuing. Pennsylvania and Delaware were both "Not Yet" on the OT Compact's application page (source: OT Compact, Application and Map).
  • Parent notice. Delaware's rule restates the Title I duty to tell parents, on request, whether a teacher is "teaching under emergency status" (source: Delaware Administrative Code, 1506 Emergency Certificate). A fully licensed hire avoids that conversation.

How does FocusedEDU get credentialed educators into your seats faster?

FocusedEDU presents educators whose files are finished before you meet them. Automated credentialing, background checks and documentation are handled before a candidate ever reaches you, so every professional we present is ready to work. Automated credentialing cuts hiring time in half while weeding out unqualified candidates before they reach your desk.

The work runs on VerifAI, our AI-powered credentialing platform. It reads every clearance and certificate on upload, our credentialing team approves each one, and each expiration date is tracked from then on. Each candidate is presented once every required credential is approved and unexpired and the start date is confirmed. You interview and choose. Temp-to-perm lets you evaluate a professional on the job before you commit to a permanent hire, at no additional cost to your school. The educators we recruit for you are never shared with a competing school, and we have partnered with K-12 schools for 12 years.

If you have a special education, related services or classroom seat that an out-of-state educator could fill this semester, send us the opening with the role, school and start date. If you want to walk through which route fits your state first, book a call.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an emergency permit and a provisional license?
faqs.a: An emergency permit is requested by the district for a vacancy it cannot fill and usually lasts 1 school year. In Pennsylvania it runs to the last day of summer school. A provisional license is a longer bridge for a new hire who is finishing requirements: New Jersey's lasts up to 2 years and can be renewed once, and Maryland's conditional license lasts up to 5 years.

faqs.q: Which states are in the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact?
faqs.a: The Council of State Governments' compact map marks 14 states as enacted: Alabama, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Kansas, Kentucky, Nebraska, Nevada, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Utah, Virginia and Washington. Mississippi enacted it with material language changes and was not admitted. A teacher needs an unencumbered license, not a provisional, substitute or temporary one, to use it.

faqs.q: How does teacher license reciprocity work between states?
faqs.a: There is no automatic national reciprocity. Each state grants its own license to an out-of-state teacher who meets its rule. New Jersey asks for a valid out-of-state standard certificate and 2 effective years of teaching within 3 consecutive years. Pennsylvania's Pathway 1 asks for 2 years of experience on a professional out-of-state certificate. Maryland issues a 2-year Temporary Professional License while an out-of-state teacher finishes Maryland's tests. Teachers from Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact states get a streamlined review in other member states.

faqs.q: Can a special education teacher work on an emergency permit?
faqs.a: Not under federal rules. 34 CFR 300.156(c) requires public school special education teachers to hold full state certification that has not been waived on an emergency, temporary or provisional basis. The exception is an alternate route program with intensive supervision and a time limit of 3 years. Maryland's conditional special education license is built on that model.

faqs.q: Is the ASLP-IC live for school speech-language pathologists?
faqs.a: Partly. The ASLP-IC Commission reports 37 jurisdictions have enacted the compact, but registration for compact privileges is open in 6 states: Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Ohio, Tennessee and West Virginia. In other member states, a speech-language pathologist still needs that state's license until it begins issuing privileges.

faqs.q: Can a school psychologist use the school psychologist compact yet?
faqs.a: Not yet. The Interstate Compact for School Psychologists map lists 10 enacting states, including Delaware and Maryland, but its own site answers the question "No, not at this time" because it is still becoming operational (Council of State Governments). Colorado reports the commissioners met in January 2026 to start writing rules. Until then, school psychologists apply through each state's education department.

faqs.q: Can an out-of-state teacher start before Pennsylvania clearances come back?
faqs.a: Pennsylvania permits, but does not require, a provisional hire for a single period of up to 90 days while checks are pending. The applicant must have applied for the checks, affirm in writing that they are not disqualified, and may not work alone with children. All 3 reports must be no more than 5 years old at the time of hire.
